definitions.explanation: A real number that cannot be expressed as a ratio of two integers — examples include π (pi), √2, and e. Contrasted with rational numbers ({有理数|ゆうりすう}).

examples.japanese: {円周率|えんしゅうりつ}は{無理数|むりすう}だ。
{無理数|むりすう}は{小数|しょうすう}で{表|あらわ}すと{無限|むげん}に{続|つづ}く。
examples.english: When written in decimal form, an irrational number continues infinitely.

examples.japanese: √2が{無理数|むりすう}であることは{古代|こだい}ギリシャの{時代|じだい}にすでに{証明|しょうめい}されていた。
examples.english: That √2 is irrational was already proven back in ancient Greek times.

notes:
Compound of {無理|むり} (impossible, unreasonable) + {数|すう} (number) — literally "unreasonable number," a calque of the European term. Used in mathematics from middle school onward.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {無理数|むりすう}と{有理数|ゆうりすう}: irrational and rational numbers
- {無理数|むりすう}を{含|ふく}む: to include irrational numbers
- {無限|むげん}{小数|しょうすう}の{無理数|むりすう}: irrational number as an infinite decimal

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {有理数|ゆうりすう}: rational number — direct antonym; expressible as a fraction
- {実数|じっすう}: real number — the broader category containing both rational and irrational numbers
- {虚数|きょすう}: imaginary number — numbers involving √-1, outside the real-number line
